findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing file, permission denied, or I/O error
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or absent file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError::Io> and use .map_err(|e| PacketError::Io(e))

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are raw index accesses into a Vec with no length guard
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line with fewer than 2 fields panics at runtime via index out of bounds
findings.fix: use get(0) and get(1) with .ok_or(PacketError::Malformed) or restructure with split_once

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() - both the index and the unwrap are unchecked
findings.failure_mode: line missing second field panics on index; non-numeric second field panics on parse
findings.fix: use split_once(',') with .ok_or(PacketError::Malformed), then parse value with .map_err(|_| PacketError::InvalidValue)

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 is a lossy down-cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range, producing incorrect domain data with no error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| PacketError::ValueOutOfBounds) to catch out-of-range conversions

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds side-effect I/O inside data-processing map closure
findings.failure_mode: parsing logic leaks logging side effects, making the function non-deterministic, untestable, and violating Data/Calculations/Actions separation
findings.fix: remove println entirely; if diagnostic logging is needed, isolate it in a shell-layer action function that calls a pure parsing core

findings.problem: load_packets fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, logging (println), allocation, and domain construction into one function
findings.failure_mode: no pure parsing core exists; shell and core are inseparable, preventing reuse, testing, and verification of the parsing logic independently of I/O
findings.fix: extract a pure fn parse_packet(line: &str) -> Result<Record, PacketError> and have load_packets call it after reading the file with proper error propagation

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no Result type; all failures are expressed as panics
findings.failure_mode: any error (I/O, malformed input, parse failure, range overflow) collapses to panic instead of returning structured typed errors that callers can handle
findings.fix: define enum PacketError { Io(io::Error), Malformed, InvalidValue, ValueOutOfBounds, Allocation } and change signature to -> Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError>

findings.problem: text.lines().map(...).collect() allocates an unbounded Vec with no capacity cap or try_reserve
findings.failure_mode: large or unbounded input file causes unbounded heap allocation, enabling OOM attacks with no domain limit
findings.fix: accept a max_packets: usize parameter, call out.try_reserve(max_packets).map_err(|_| PacketError::Allocation)?, and reject lines exceeding the cap with a TooMany error

findings.problem: raw String primitives from CSV split cross the parse boundary into domain Record without fallible smart constructors; name is accepted as a free-form String with no validation
findings.failure_mode: invalid or empty record names (e.g. whitespace-only, zero-length) are accepted as valid domain values, violating data validity by construction
findings.fix: create a parse_boundary function: fn parse_name(raw: &str) -> Result<String, PacketError> that trims and rejects empty strings, and use split_once(',') instead of split/collect

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() builds a full Vec<String> from every line just to extract two fields
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocation per line; each CSV line allocates a Vec plus N String copies before discarding them
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(PacketError::Malformed)? to get (_name, value_str) directly, then parse value_str.trim() without intermediate collection

findings.problem: Record.name is a raw String with no constraints encoded in the type
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct Record with empty, null, or otherwise invalid names; the domain invariant on name is not enforced at the type level
findings.fix: introduce a newtype struct RecordName(String) with a smart constructor fn try_from_name(raw: &str) -> Result<RecordName, PacketError> and use it in Record

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated or implied parsing-throughput performance claim
no profiler evidence (flame graph, perf profile) identifying the hot path or allocation hotspots
no allocation audit (e.g. dlmalloc stats, jemalloc profiling) showing per-record allocation count
no second-ring evidence (Valgrind massif, cachegrind) for memory traffic or cache behavior
no command-truth evidence: no recorded baseline and new-number benchmark run
no clippy/gate command evidence for strict source linting
residual_risk: Review is static-only with no commands run. The crate has 11 BLOCKER findings covering panic surfaces (unwrap on I/O, parse, and indexing), lossy casts, hidden I/O, shell-core fusion, missing typed error taxonomy, unbounded allocation, intermediate allocations, raw-primitive domain types, and missing parse-boundary validation. All are independently reproducible defects that will panic or misbehave on untrusted input. Without the mandatory gate commands (cargo fmt --check, cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo test), residual risk includes undiscovered clippy warnings and compilation failures.
